header: Date: 2026-09-10 | Time: 10:00 PDT | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Lunaris Head of ML), Ethan Moore (Lunaris SRE), Angela Park (Lunaris Product)
summary: Weekly POC sync focusing on unit economics. Reviewed initial benchmark results, observed caching savings, discussed batching/latency tradeoffs. Agreed next steps: run 1M-token benchmark, share cost model, schedule Dedicated canary. Some transcription errors on model names noted.
topics: Caching impact (prefix/KV cache) and TTL tradeoffs
Hosted vs Dedicated cost and fallback policies
transcript: 00:00 - Maya Chen: alright everyone thanks for joining, uh this is the weekly POC cost econ sync for Lunaris, um quick roll call?
00:08 - Priya Singh: hey Priya here, head of ML at Lunaris
00:11 - Ethan Moore: Ethan, SRE
00:13 - Angela Park: Angela, product
00:15 - Daniel Ortiz: daniel from redwood se, hi
00:20 - Maya Chen: cool, real quick agenda - go over the benchmark numbers you sent, demo a couple cache/batch tweaks, talk hosted vs dedicated economics and next steps

02:05 - Priya Singh: thanks, yeah on the numbers - we saw your initial tokens per second and cost per token table, um couple questions: how are you measuring token/sec/$? it looked like the hosted run had lower latencies but higher cost per token which is surprising

02:40 - Daniel Ortiz: yeah so basically token/sec/$ is throughput divided by cost per minute normalized; note hosted includes multi-tenant overhead, and our measurement includes average cloud vcpu+gpu time; there may be some variance in the first-pass numbers
03:25 - Ethan Moore: i also noticed the cache savings row - was that prefix cache only or kv cache too? the spreadsheet says "prefix cache" but our logs show repeated history patterns

03:50 - Daniel Ortiz: good call - that run was prefix-only, kay vee cache (KV cache) was not enabled in that pass, we did a short run with KV enabled and saw roughly 18-22% token cost reduction for median seq lengths ~120
04:30 - Priya Singh: 18-22% is promising, what about cold-starts or TTL evictions, llc?

05:00 - Daniel Ortiz: TTL tradeoff is key - shorter TTL reduces memory but increases misses; for your workload with high session re-use we recommend a 1h TTL to get most savings, but we'll test 30m vs 1h in the 1M-token run
06:10 - Maya Chen: on batching, we saw some configs where batch=32 boosted tokens/sec but tail latency jumped to 450ms which may break your UI SLOs, what is acceptable?
06:35 - Angela Park: ideally p95 under 300ms for interactive parts, some background jobs can tolerate higher
07:00 - Daniel Ortiz: right so tradeoff is throughput vs p95. We typically recommend dynamic batching with a small max batch (8-16) for interactive endpoints and larger for async processes
08:12 - Priya Singh: how does Redwood Dedicated change the math? is the unit cost lower at high sustained qps?

08:35 - Maya Chen: yes Dedicated has reserved GPU pools and lower per-token unit cost at scale because you avoid multi-tenant overhead and can pin model versions; but there's a commit cost - so it depends on utilization
09:05 - Ethan Moore: can you run a model variant with quantization to drop perf cost? we saw in notes about quant profiles

09:22 - Daniel Ortiz: absolutely - q4f16 and int8 variants can reduce memory and improve throughput; quality regressions are small for your prompt set but we'll include a regression eval in the next run

11:10 - Priya Singh: about the cost model spreadsheet: some names got transcribed oddly - 'redwood dedicate' instead of 'Redwood Dedicated' and 'kay vee cache' - no biggie just want to ensure we share canonical terms
12:00 - Maya Chen: noted, we'll send a cleaned deck. also we'll include a column for tokens/sec/$ per model variant and per deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private)
14:40 - Angela Park: curious about fallback policies - if Dedicated saturates, can requests route to hosted seamlessly with same model?
15:05 - Daniel Ortiz: yes we have smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible variants; latency will differ but app can set policies to prefer latency or cost and we can do A/B canary
18:20 - Ethan Moore: security question quick - for Private/VPC tests we need SSO and audit logs, you mentioned KMS integration earlier? any blockers?
18:45 - Maya Chen: we support KMS/HSM for key management, SAML SSO, and audit logs. For the pilot we'll provide SOC2 snapshot and a short integration guide - Daniel will attach the security pack
22:00 - Priya Singh: back to economics, can you explain the tokens/sec/$ calc real quick so our finance folks can follow?

22:25 - Daniel Ortiz: sure - tokens/sec/$ = (tokens_processed / total_time_seconds) / (cost for that run in USD). We normalize across runs by using same probe load and include infra amortization for Dedicated runs
25:30 - Priya Singh: ok makes sense, one ask - can you run a 1M token run with traffic shaped to our median and 95th seq lengths and include batch sizes 8/16/32 and KV TTL 30m/1h?
26:00 - Daniel Ortiz: yes we'll do that; expect results in about 4-5 business days, we'll push raw logs and the summarized cost sheet

30:10 - Maya Chen: recap: Daniel runs benchmark, Maya sends cleaned cost deck + security docs, Priya confirms SLOs, Ethan sets up VPC peering window. Schedule Dedicated canary next week pending results
31:50 - Priya Singh: one more question - how do you measure prefix cache hit rate vs kv miss? we want per-endpoint breakdown

32:10 - Daniel Ortiz: we'll include endpoint-level metrics: hit rate, miss latency, tokens saved, and money saved. We'll also add a small eval harness to detect hallucination changes post-quantization
38:00 - Angela Park: great, also please include suggested rollout plan (canary %, rollback triggers) in the doc
39:15 - Maya Chen: will do. any other blockers?
40:00 - Ethan Moore: just confirming timeline for peering - aiming 2026-09-14, i'll update calendar
41:12 - Priya Singh: thanks everyone, excited. we'll review results and decide on Dedicated commit after the 1M run
42:05 - Maya Chen: perfect, thanks team, we'll follow up with artifacts. meeting end
44:30 - (call ended)
